business_problem: ZEISS Medical Technology needed a faster way for ophthalmologists and clinical staff to answer patient questions about elective treatments, while keeping every response accurate, empathetic, current, and grounded in approved medical-technology content.
solution_summary: BCG worked with ZEISS Medical Technology to build a proof-of-concept generative-AI application for ophthalmology practices. After assessing a hundred possible GenAI use cases, the joint team selected patient-inquiry response generation and built the first version in eight weeks. The application ingests patient-submitted content forms and self-test forms, retrieves relevant facts from a library of approved Zeiss marketing and patient materials, and uses Azure OpenAI with LangChain, vector databases, and LLM agent techniques to draft responses. BCG and the Zeiss AI team refined the workflow in agile iterations using customer insights and tester feedback, while responsible-AI guardrails and human validation checked output quality. The result is a validated assistant that can produce personalized, patient-ready answers while staying grounded in approved source content.

solution_components.name: Azure OpenAI
solution_components.role: Provides the foundation-model inference used to generate draft responses to patient questions.

solution_components.name: LangChain
solution_components.role: Coordinates the prompt and application workflow between patient inputs, retrieved content, and model output generation.

solution_components.name: large language model (LLM) agent technologies
solution_components.role: Guide the response-generation logic so the application can answer patient questions in a structured way.

solution_components.name: Vector databases
solution_components.role: Store approved Zeiss materials so the application can retrieve grounded source content before generating answers.

data_flow: Patient-submitted content forms and self-test forms enter the application, which retrieves relevant passages from approved Zeiss marketing and patient materials stored for RAG. LangChain and LLM agent logic orchestrate the workflow, Azure OpenAI generates draft responses, and validated outputs are returned to practices as patient-ready answers or drafts for review.
business_outcome: ZEISS Medical Technology validated that a GenAI assistant could answer patient inquiries with high quality while reducing manual drafting for practices; test users were strongly positive, and with settings customization 93% of responses were judged ready to send without edits.
